Dartmoor by Motorcycle: Wild Moorland Riding

Dartmoor is Devon's dramatic upland — a granite plateau rising above the surrounding farmland, dotted with ancient tors, crossed by clear rivers, and populated by wild ponies and sheep. The riding roads across the moor are atmospheric, varied, and unlike anything else in southern England.

The Key Roads

  • B3212 Moretonhampstead to Princetown: The classic Dartmoor crossing. Open moorland with granite tors visible in every direction. The road passes Two Bridges (a historic meeting point) and continues to Princetown — home of Dartmoor Prison.
  • B3357 Tavistock to Two Bridges: A flowing west-east crossing through the heart of the moor. Merrivale stone rows and standing stones are visible from the road.
  • Haytor to Widecombe: The road past Haytor Rocks (one of Dartmoor's most famous tors) drops down into the pretty village of Widecombe-in-the-Moor through classic moorland scenery.

Hidden Gems

  • Dartmeet: Where the East and West Dart rivers meet in a wooded valley. An ancient clapper bridge crosses the river. Beautiful but accessed via narrow lanes.
  • Postbridge Clapper Bridge: A medieval stone slab bridge crossing the East Dart River. An iconic Dartmoor sight right beside the B3212.
  • Grimspound: A Bronze Age settlement visible from the road between Widecombe and Moretonhampstead. 3,000 years of history in a moorland setting.

Hazards and Tips

  • Livestock: Dartmoor ponies, sheep, and cattle roam freely across the moor and onto roads. They have no road sense and can appear suddenly from mist. Slow down in areas marked with livestock warning signs.
  • Weather: Dartmoor creates its own weather. Mist can descend rapidly and visibility can drop to metres. If mist comes down, slow right down, use dipped headlights, and follow the road markings carefully.
  • Narrow lanes: Many Dartmoor lanes are single-track with high stone walls and limited visibility. Approach blind corners cautiously.
  • Military ranges: Parts of Dartmoor are used by the military. Red flags flying means the range is active — stick to public roads.
Dartmoor is best experienced slowly. The moor reveals itself gradually — a standing stone glimpsed through mist, a wild pony silhouetted on a tor, a medieval bridge over a rushing stream. These are the moments that make Dartmoor unique. Rush across it and you'll miss them all.

Pubs and Traditions

Dartmoor's pubs are legendary. The Warren House Inn, at 434m the highest pub in southern England, sits alone on the moor between Postbridge and Moretonhampstead. The fire in the bar has supposedly been burning continuously since 1845. The pub serves good food and the views from the beer garden across the moor are vast.

Widecombe-in-the-Moor, made famous by the folk song about Uncle Tom Cobley, is a quintessential Dartmoor village. The 14th-century church, known as the Cathedral of the Moor, towers above the village green. The café and village shop make it a natural rest stop mid-ride. keyTakeaways: The B3212 from Moretonhampstead to Princetown is the classic Dartmoor crossing, with granite tors in every direction.
Wild ponies, sheep and cattle roam freely onto the roads and can appear suddenly from mist, so slow down near livestock signs.
Dartmoor creates its own weather; mist can descend rapidly and cut visibility to metres.
Highlights include Haytor Rocks, the medieval Postbridge clapper bridge and the Bronze Age settlement at Grimspound.

faq.q: How dangerous is the livestock on Dartmoor?
faq.a: Dartmoor ponies, sheep and cattle roam freely across the moor and onto the roads. They have no road sense and can appear suddenly, especially out of mist. Slow right down in areas marked with livestock warning signs and give animals a wide berth. Collisions are a real risk, particularly at dawn and dusk, so ride at a pace that lets you stop for an animal in the road.

faq.q: What should I do if mist comes down?
faq.a: Dartmoor creates its own weather, and mist can descend rapidly, dropping visibility to just a few metres. If it comes down, slow right down, use dipped headlights and follow the road markings carefully. Do not press on at speed hoping it will clear. The combination of poor visibility, wandering livestock and narrow lanes makes caution essential when the moor clouds over.

faq.q: Which is the best road to ride across Dartmoor?
faq.a: The B3212 from Moretonhampstead to Princetown is the classic Dartmoor crossing, with open moorland and granite tors visible in every direction, passing Two Bridges and the Postbridge clapper bridge. The B3357 from Tavistock to Two Bridges is a flowing west-east alternative past the Merrivale stone rows. Ride both slowly to take in the standing stones, tors and wild ponies.

faq.q: Where can I stop for a break?
faq.a: The Warren House Inn, at 434m the highest pub in southern England, sits alone on the moor between Postbridge and Moretonhampstead, with a fire that has supposedly burned continuously since 1845 and vast views from the beer garden. Widecombe-in-the-Moor, with its 14th-century Cathedral of the Moor church, has a cafe and village shop that make a natural mid-ride stop.
